message:
Plain words: the hopper carries half-full to stay inside weight while keeping the outlet too big to jam, Manager. The 150 mm outlet area 0.0177 m2 from the outlet area calc (E69) over the 20 L steep wedge holding 30 kg max from the hopper payload calc (E10) run at 15 kg trips from the hopper filling simulation (E11) is fist-size against shoe-box load, so everyday scale says gravity plus screw should drain, with the steep-wall mass-flow need from the Jenike sources behind the wedge hopper (C4) leaving arching as the named bench test, and total 46.0 kg against 60.0 kg from the updated mass sum (E62) keeps carry volume inside mass.

Plain words: the chain meets soil shallow so it scoops rather than bulldozes, and basalt will still eat plain edge, Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead and Power Structure and Integration Lead please note. Ladder incline near 30 deg to soil with replaceable steel teeth keeps kerf cut 11.0 N from the kerf scaling calc (E64) against 294 N traction, about 1 kg push on a person-scale machine, but Black Point-1 (BP-1, meaning crushed basalt lunar simulant) abrasion means edge wear stays as bench test, not calculation.

Plain words: the metered pour plus camera tag is what lets a blind reverse dump hit the bin, Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead I confirm your stall-avoidance source for my drive. I take from the Systems, devices, and/or methods regarding excavating (E57) and its twin CA2784416C patent (E56) the finding that crowd backs off on hoist stall, which for my ladder plus screw means current-limit foldback plus 0.600 s reverse from the tag align and backout simulation (E58) protects the 16.4 W ladder power from the ladder power estimate (E59); pivot 0.550 m clears 0.400 m lip by 0.150 m from the tip dump clearance check (E51) with align 0.030 to 0.040 m, finger width against 0.150 m mouth, and level-only 15 kg trips hold factor 1.69 per the Skid-Steer Safety rule (E47). Ready, because cut, carry, and dump survive traction, mass, and tip checks with only arching and wear bench tests left.
